messages.content: You are a precise information extraction system. You only output valid JSON.

Extract entities, events and event arguments from the document.

Entity types:
- Person: a named or described human individual or group of people
- Organization: a company, army, government body, team, party or other organised group
- Location: a geographic place: country, city, region, body of water, battlefield, etc.
- Building: a man-made structure or facility: hotel, fort, bridge, airport, etc.
- Product: a man-made object or product: vehicle, ship, aircraft, weapon model, etc.
- Art: a creative work: book, film, song, painting, etc.
- Other: any other named thing relevant to events (e.g. nationalities, named events, ideologies)

Entity annotation rules:
- Annotate named entities AND other mentions that refer to them: nominal phrases ("the plane", "the war"), pronouns ("he", "they"), and nationality/group words ("British", "Ottomans").
- Numbers, quantities, ordinals and durations ("13", "two", "3rd", "two days") are entities of type Other.
- Annotate every occurrence, including repeated mentions of the same entity.
- Nationality or group words are typed by what they refer to: a country/place -> Location, an army/state/organisation -> Organization, a people -> Person.

Event types:
- Attack: An agent physically assaults or launches a violent attack on a target (bombing, ambush, raid, shooting, assault). (e.g. attack, assaulted, ambushed, bombing)
- Military_operation: Organised armed conflict between forces: a war, battle, campaign, siege or military operation as a whole. (e.g. war, battle, fought, campaign)
- Conquering: An agent takes control of a place or group by force (capture, seize, conquer, occupy). (e.g. captured, conquer, seized, taken)
- Killing: A killer causes the death of a victim (an agent is responsible for the death). (e.g. killed, killing, murdered, massacre)
- Death: Someone dies, with focus on the death itself rather than on a killer. (e.g. died, death, dead, deaths)
- Bodily_harm: Someone is physically injured or wounded. (e.g. injured, wounded, injuries, hurt)
- Catastrophe: A natural or man-made disaster happens (storm, flood, earthquake, crash, fire, accident). (e.g. hurricane, storm, flood, earthquake)
- Destroying: Something is destroyed completely (destroyed, demolished, sunk, burned down). (e.g. destroyed, destruction, demolished, sank)
- Damaging: Something is damaged but not completely destroyed. (e.g. damage, damaged, struck, battered)
- Statement: A speaker communicates a message (says, states, announces, describes, reports). (e.g. said, stated, announced, described)
- Change_of_leadership: Leadership or control of a polity or organisation changes (election, coup, revolution, ousting, independence, replacement of a leader). (e.g. elected, coup, revolution, ousted)
- Arriving: An agent arrives at or reaches a place. (e.g. arrived, reached, entered, landed)

Trigger annotation rules:
- A trigger is the single word (sometimes a short phrase) that most clearly expresses the event; it can be a verb ("attacked") or a noun ("attack", "war", "fires").
- Annotate EVERY occurrence: if the same event is mentioned several times ("the fires ... the fires ..."), list each occurrence as a separate entry.
- Only annotate the 12 event types below; ignore other kinds of events.
- Disambiguation:
  * Military_operation = a war, battle, campaign or siege as a whole; Attack = one specific assault, bombing, raid, shelling or ambush.
  * Conquering = capturing or taking control of a place or group (captured, seized, took, defeated and occupied).
  * Killing = someone or something kills (killed, massacre, slain, executed); Death = the dying itself (died, death, dead, fatalities).
  * Catastrophe = the disaster event itself (storm, hurricane, fire, flood, crash, accident); Destroying = something is completely destroyed; Damaging = something is damaged but not destroyed.
  * Bodily_harm = injury or wounding (injured, wounded, injuries).

Argument roles:
Event type Attack: An agent physically assaults or launches a violent attack on a target (bombing, ambush, raid, shooting, assault).
Roles:
- Agent: the attacker
- Patient: the target being attacked
- Location: where the attack happens
- Consequence: the result of the attack (e.g. casualties, what was gained)

Argument annotation rules:
- Arguments may be anywhere in the document, not only in the trigger's sentence.
- Copy the SHORTEST span that fully identifies the argument: prefer a name ("Seneca") over a longer phrase ("the Seneca in particular"); for people counts keep the number phrase ("30 such individuals").
- A role may have several arguments; omit a role if the document does not mention it.
- Consequence/Loss/Message/Details roles are usually clauses or longer phrases; copy them as written.

The 2014–15 Australian bushfire season was expected to have the potential for many fires in eastern Australia after lower than expected rainfall was received in many areas. Authorities released warnings in the early spring that the season could be particularly bad. Warmer and drier weather conditions were experienced during winter and extended into 2015, due to a developing El Niño event. Sydney was on track to record its hottest autumn on record and only had one fifth of the average rainfall in May. Adelaide recorded sixteen consecutive days of in May 2014. Queensland sweltered through a heatwave, with record October temperatures being set in many towns through the state. New October records included Toowoomba with, St George with, Amberley with and Roma with. Throughout 2014 and the first 6 months of 2015, 18 fires were declared " national disasters " affecting a total of 68 local government areas across New South Wales, South Australia, Victoria and the Northern Territory. During an 8-day period starting on 1 August, 114 bush and grass fires burned through of the Clarence Valley and Kempsey local government areas. Five houses were destroyed and a further eight were extensively damaged during the blazes. Eight non-residential buildings and four vehicles were also destroyed in the blazes. A number of these fires were caused by escaped private hazard reduction burns. Fires started near Katoomba in the Blue Mountains just as heatwave conditions commenced in the area on 1 November. The fire dropped over an escarpment and into inaccessible bushland. One house was destroyed and a second house damaged along Cliff Drive after 60 people were evacuated from the area.

### Example 2
Document:
The Black Sunday bushfires were a series of bushfires that broke out across South Australia on 2 January 1955. Extreme morning temperatures coupled with strong north-westerly winds contributed to the breakout of numerous fires in the Adelaide Hills, Jamestown, Waterloo, Kingston and Millicent. Most were caused by sparks from powerlines downed by the wind. around 1,000 emergency fire service volunteers from 60 brigades were tasked to the fires, but were overwhelmed. at 10am, the efs head office requested urgent public assistance. Around 2,500 citizens volunteered. The fires were contained by 9:30pm, thanks largely to a fortuitous change in the weather and widespread public assistance. The fires resulted in two deaths, destroyed 40 homes and numerous other buildings, and caused more than four million dollars ' worth of property damage, most notably the destruction of the Governor's summer residence at Marble Hill. Governor Robert George, his family and staff were lucky to escape with their lives. The Premier, Sir Thomas Playford, also narrowly escaped death, sheltering with five other men in a patch of hoed earth near Cherryville. The burnt area was estimated at as much as stretching from One Tree Hill to Strathalbyn; however, other sources put the area at closer to.

As many as 3,000 firefighters including 800 Washington National Guard members were deployed to fight the fires. the 17th field artillery brigade of the united states army also deployed 200 soldiers from joint base unk to help fight the fires. Because of the enormous extent of the fire activity, for the first time in Washington state history, officials asked residents to volunteer to assist in fighting the wildfires. The 2013 New South Wales bushfires were a series of bushfires in Australia across the state of New South Wales primarily starting, or becoming notable, on 13 October 2013; followed by the worst of the fires beginning in the Greater Blue Mountains Area on 16 and 17 October 2013. High fuel loads, coupled with warm, dry and windy weather, provided dangerous conditions which fuelled the fires. at the peak of the fires, on the morning of 18 october, over 100 fires were burning across the state. The Premier of New South Wales Barry O'Farrell declared a state of emergency on 20 October, empowering firefighters to evict residents and demolish fire-affected buildings. The fires are the worst in New South Wales since the 1960s., 248 houses and other structures were destroyed across the state. Two fatalities were attributed to the fires. It was estimated that claims will exceed 94 million.
